sources.entry: pretalx - Web-based event management, including running a Call for Papers, reviewing submissions, and scheduling talks. Exports and imports for various related tools. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python

summary.one_liner: pretalx is a self-hostable, web-based conference planning tool that covers call for participation, submission reviewing, scheduling, and speaker communication.
summary.what_it_does: pretalx handles a conference's submission process with a configurable Call for Participation that supports custom questions, tracks, and session types. It provides collaborative reviewing, scoring, and team-based selection of submissions. It supports building, versioning, and releasing schedules across rooms and days, with a public agenda and per-speaker views. It also sends templated, queued emails and invitations, collects post-event feedback, and lets speakers upload slides and organisers embed recordings. The README also mentions a documented REST API, an extensible plugin system, and internationalisation.
use_cases: run a call for papers for a conference
build and publish a conference schedule
email speakers about their submission status
how_to_run: Self-host following the administrator documentation at docs.pretalx.org (Docker-based or manual setup)
Alternatively, use the public instance at pretalx.com
notable: Covers the full conference lifecycle from call for papers through published schedule
Documented REST API and extensible plugin system
Versioned schedule releases across rooms and days
Actively developed with regular releases and 100% test coverage CI gate
Hosted public instance at pretalx.com available as an alternative to self-hosting
caveats: Self-hosting requires PostgreSQL and Redis alongside Python 3.12+
Full setup details are in external documentation rather than the README
